walkthroughs.body_html:
Muslims believe Allah sent thousands of prophets — 25 are named in the Qur'an.

Key prophets include Adam, Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Dawud (David), Isa (Jesus) and finally Muhammad ﷺ — the Seal of the Prophets (Qur'an 33:40).

All prophets brought the same core message: worship one God.

Muslims believe Allah revealed several holy books (Kutub):

- Tawrat (Torah) to Musa
- Zabur (Psalms) to Dawud
- Injil (Gospel) to Isa
- Qur'an to Muhammad ﷺ

The Qur'an, revealed over 23 years from 610 CE, is the final, unchanged word of Allah.

Angels (Malaikah) are made of light and serve Allah perfectly.

Jibril (Gabriel) brought revelation. Mikail (Michael) brings sustenance. Israfil will blow the trumpet at the end of time. Izrail takes souls at death.

On Yawm al-Qiyamah all are judged — bound for Jannah (paradise) or Jahannam (hell).

Jibril

Izrail

mcqs.q: How many prophets are named in the Qur'an?
What is the difference between Sunni and Shia Islam?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Sunnis and Shias believe in different gods.
They split over who should lead the Muslim community after Muhammad: Sunnis accepted Abu Bakr and elected caliphs; Shias believed leadership should follow Muhammad's bloodline through Ali.
Sunnis follow the Quran and Shias follow the Bible.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
